pieces.opens_with: The same chocolate can set six different ways, and only one of them snaps. Here is the whole video in three sentences. Chocolate snaps because its fat is set in one chosen crystal, called form five. Bread rises because living yeast breathes carbon dioxide into a web of gluten. And steak browns because sugars and amino acids react on its hot, dry surface.

pieces.opens_with: Why does seared meat taste so good?

And that is all three: a square of chocolate, a loaf and a steak. A fat that picks one crystal out of six, a fungus that breathes, and a reaction that only happens where it is hot and dry. If you have made it this far, you now know more about your dinner than most of the people who cooked it for you, which is a lovely thing to know and a terrible thing to say out loud at the table. Keep it to yourself. Eat the crust first. Let the chocolate melt on your tongue, not in your hand. And next time, we will find out what happens inside an egg, which turns out to be stranger than anything in this video. Thank you for watching all the way to the end. If there is a food you have always wondered about, tell us in the comments, and it might become one of the questions.
